newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes limp to lower prices on Iraq deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes limp to lower prices on Iraq deal.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices deflated Monday on word the United Nations sealed a key humanitarian aid plan with Iraq, possibly pushing the start date for renewed oil sales to late July or early August.

Just minutes ahead of the NYMEX open, reports landed quoting the U.N. coordinator in Baghdad, Staffan De Mistura, as saying negotiations with Iraq ended successfully. Now, the path is clear for submission of the plan for U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan's approval, and later the formulation of a new pricing formula for oil sales contracts.

Even though Iraq received U.N. approval for a second round of "oil-for-food" sales from June 8, there have been no new liftings pending approval of the aid plan. Traders said it appeared that exports are in the offing, following Monday's developments.
"I'd like to hear the confirmation from more people, but for the most part it looks like there is no problem for resuming the sales," said a trader.
August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing ended around 30 cents lower at $18.95-19.05 a barrel, with the August/September roll at minus 16-18 cents.
Cash business quietly traded at steady levels for the grades, with Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James continuing to find a support at 20 cent premiums to the benchmark.
Traders said the biggest movement in grades saw West Texas Sour/Midland talk late at a $1.25-1.20 discount, bolstered by active refiner buying.
Deals were also seen at steady levels for Midland/WTI. WTI/Cushing Postings Plus lost some ground on the Aug/Sep roll, but for the most part little excitement was noted.
"There was the normal Monday business cycle, and combined with people watching the NYMEX for Iraq reaction, there was not much moving in the U.S. Gulf," said a cash dealer.
